request.spec:
Periods can be generated: a from-date and a to-date and a button create one period per calendar
month from the from-date's month to the to-date's month, each running from the first to the last
day of its month (February ends on the 28th or 29th), named yyyy-mm, each written as PERIOD_ADDED.
A month whose name is already a period, or whose days overlap a period on the sheet, is left out
and the others are still made. Show how many were made. A to-date before the from-date is refused
with an error.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Periods can be generated: a from-date and a to-date and a button create one period per calendar
month from the from-date's month to the to-date's month, each running from the first to the last
day of its month (February ends on the 28th or 29th), named yyyy-mm, each written as PERIOD_ADDED.
A month whose name is already a period, or whose days overlap a period on the sheet, is left out
and the others are still made. Show how many were made. A to-date before the from-date is refused
with an error.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Periods can now be generated by month, and all 4 acceptance tests pass under `bin/e2e`.

**Server:** I added a new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{sheet}/periods/generate`, defined in `periods/generate.POST.yml`. It runs three steps:
- **Check the dates** (`ValidateGeneratePeriods`): a to-date before the from-date, or a date that isn't valid, is refused with the existing period error, so nothing is written. A blank from-date means the sheet's today.
- **Make the periods** (`GeneratePeriods`): one period per calendar month, from the from-date's month to the to-date's month. Each is named `yyyy-mm` and runs from the 1st to the last day of the month, so February ends on the 28th or 29th as the year requires. A month is skipped if a period already has that name or overlaps its days; the other months are still made. Each new period writes its own `PERIOD_ADDED` audit line, in the same format as adding a period by hand.
- **Reply** (`RespondWithGeneratedPeriods`): returns how many were made and the sheet's full list of periods.

**Front end:** the Periods panel has a new form with a from field (`period-generate-from`), a to field (`period-generate-to`) and a button (`period-generate`). After a run it shows how many were made (`period-generated`); a refused run shows `period-generate-error`. The count and the error are cleared when either field is changed or the button is pressed again.

No database change was needed, because generated periods are stored like ones added by hand.
